name: Rajma Chawal
summary: Kidney beans simmered in a spiced onion-tomato gravy, served over rice. A North Indian weeknight staple.

ingredients.name: chili powder (or cayenne for more heat)
red kidney beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Cook the rice: 300 g rice with 600 mL water, simmered covered for 15 minutes, then rested 5 minutes.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the bay leaf and onion and cook 8–10 minutes until deep golden. This is where most of the flavour comes from, so don't rush it.
Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then the cumin, coriander, turmeric, and chili powder for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes, mashing them, until the oil starts to separate at the edges.
Add the beans and 500 mL water. Simmer 15–20 minutes, mashing a few beans against the side of the pot to thicken the gravy.
Stir in the garam masala and salt. Serve over the rice.

glutenFree.notes: Beans, tomatoes, rice, and spices are naturally gluten-free. Some spice blends are cut with wheat flour. Check the garam masala label.

budgetNotes: Rajma is better the next day and freezes well.
Dried kidney beans are cheaper still, but they must be soaked overnight and boiled hard for at least 10 minutes. Undercooked kidney beans are toxic.
A spoon of plain yogurt or butter on top is traditional if you have it.
